title: Calculation of structural symmetry and applicability of small AkBlCm nanoclusters (A=Rb, Cs; B=Pb, Sn, Bi; C=Cl, Br, I) as building blocks for synthesis of larger-size nanoclusters
authors: Roman Makarevych, Igor Dmytruk, Yevhen Hrabovskyi, Iryna Pundyk, Nataliia Bashmakova, Nataliya Berezovska
abstract: In this report we analyze charasteristics of structural symmetry of small AkBlCm nanoclusters (A - Rb, Cs; B - Pb, Sn, Bi; C - Cl, Br, I), binding energies, stability, and, ultimately, applicability as building blocks for construction of larger-size nanoclusters. Preliminary spatial modeling of ternary compound nanoclusters has been carried out on the basics of geometrical approach, namely interatomic distances taken as a sums of corresponding ionic radii. The geometry optimization and binding energies of the modeled structures have been determined through quantum-chemical calculations. Geometry optimization has been performed with Gaussian09 software package using Density Functional Theory (DFT) within the generalized gradient approximation of the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) and hybrid approximation of the Becke-3-Lee-Yang-Parr (B3LYP) exchange-correlation functionals. The Stuttgart/Dresden (SDD) and Los Alamos National Laboratory 2 Double Zeta (LANL2DZ) scalar-relativistic effective basic potentials were employed throughout the calculations. As a result of these calculations, a clear relationship between the atomic radii, their ratios within the nanoclusters and their stability has been obtained and analyzed.
summary: This paper computationally investigates the structural symmetry and stability of small $	ext{A}_k	ext{B}_l	ext{C}_m$ nanoclusters using DFT. By comparing multiple cluster types, the authors establish that energetic stability is governed by the relative sizes and ratios of the constituent atoms, rather than just the absolute structural symmetry. This provides a predictive framework for designing larger, stable nanostructure building blocks.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the structural symmetry and energetic stability criteria for small AkBlCm nanoclusters to assess their viability as building blocks for synthesizing larger nanoclusters.
main_result: Energetic stability is controlled by interconnected geometrical parameters, such as the average atomic radius and the relative size matching of the constituent shells, rather than solely by structural symmetry.
method: The research employs quantum-chemical calculations using Density Functional Theory (DFT) with two different functional/basis set combinations (PBE/SDD and B3LYP/LANL2DZ) to optimize geometries and calculate binding energies.
model_or_system: The system under investigation consists of ternary compound nanoclusters of the form $	ext{A}_k	ext{B}_l	ext{C}_m$, where A={Rb, Cs}, B={Pb, Sn, Bi}, and C={Cl, Br, I}. These clusters are modeled using a core-shell stereometric structure.
key_observables: Binding energy per atom ($	ext{E}_b$), structural symmetry, average atomic radius, and shell size/atomic-radius ratios.
important_parameters: The stability trends are observed across comparisons like $	ext{Cs}_3	ext{PbI}_5$ vs $	ext{Rb}_3	ext{SnBr}_5$, suggesting stability decreases with increasing average atomic radius.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that the structural trends observed are robust across different computational protocols (PBE/SDD vs B3LYP/LANL2DZ) and that the clusters are derived from heavy-element 0D perovskite properties.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the generalized geometries and stepwise geometry optimization curves for comparative clusters such as $	ext{Cs}_3	ext{PbI}_5/	ext{Rb}_3	ext{SnBr}_5$ and $	ext{Cs}_2	ext{BiI}_5/	ext{Rb}_2	ext{BiBr}_5$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the structural symmetry and binding energies of various $	ext{A}_k	ext{B}_l	ext{C}_m$ nanoclusters, comparing results derived from two independent DFT methodologies to establish general rules governing stability based on atomic size ratios.
why_interesting: While the topic is solid-state chemistry, the rigorous use of computational methods (DFT, basis sets) to establish quantitative relationships between structural descriptors (radii ratios) and energetic stability is methodologically relevant for any field relying on first-principles material prediction.
